title: Adaptive TTL presets and event-triggered evidence exports for prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers need fine-grained, auditable control over how long interactive artifacts (prompts, model responses, request logs, and derived metrics) are retained and when those artifacts must be exported as evidence (for legal holds, compliance audits, or incident investigations). Current retention controls are coarse-grained and lack event-triggered exports and preview tooling.

Proposal: Implement an adaptive TTL system with preset profiles for common regulatory needs, plus configurable event triggers that automatically snapshot and export evidence bundles when defined conditions occur (legal_hold flag, high-risk PII detection, reg-flagged tenant activity, or retention-rule changes). The feature includes a Preview/Simulator in Console to show projected eviction timelines and sample evidence bundles before committing changes.
acceptance_criteria: Admins can choose from 4 built-in TTL presets (Short, Standard, Long, Minimal-logs) and customize per-tenant/per-route overrides for prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics
System supports declarative event triggers that create a tamper-evident evidence bundle and push to configured export targets (S3, secure FTP, downstream archive) within defined SLAs
Console exposes a retention simulator that visualizes real-world effects (eviction dates, sample counts, projected storage delta) for a selected tenant over a 90-day horizon
Retention changes are recorded in the audit log with before/after snapshots and are traceable to the user who made the change
Evidence bundles include provenance metadata (hash chain id, KMS key id, export timestamp, region) and can be fetched for at least 90 days after export
Feature passes privacy & security review and is covered by an automated test suite (unit, integration, e2e for export flow)
implementation_notes:
Architecture: extend the retention engine to accept TTL profiles per artifact type and a trigger evaluation service that listens to events from request processing (classification results, legal_hold flags, admin API updates). Evidence bundling uses streaming export to avoid memory pressure and attaches a signed manifest from Customer KMS.

Storage/sampling: support sampled retention where high-volume routes use probabilistic retention with deterministic seed per tenant to enable reproducible samples.

Performance: add lightweight counters and retention-metadata caching to avoid touching request archives on every read path. Evaluate impacts on SLOs; prefer async export worker with backpressure.

Edge cases: rolling back TTL decreases must not retroactively delete already-exported evidence.

Telemetry: add metrics for exports_pushed, export_latency_ms, simulated_eviction_impact, per-tenant_retention_delta.

Operational controls: admin can pause exports for emergency operations and re-run exports from the console.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: API spec and backend scaffolding (TTL profiles + trigger framework). Internal feature flag behind 'adaptive-ttl'
Phase 2: Console simulator UI + presets, small beta with 3 pilot customers (security review concurrent)
Phase 3: Event-triggered export worker, durable evidence manifest, KMS integration and export targets
Phase 4: Broad launch with documentation, runbook for export failures, and post-launch monitoring dashboard
open_questions: What is the canonical set of built-in presets and their default durations per artifact type? (legal/compliance to advise)
Should exports be synchronous with retention-change API calls or queued and retried asynchronously? (tradeoff: latency vs reliability)
What retention UI language reduces accidental risk for customers who may think 'Short' retains no logs at all?
Do we require signed attestations for evidence bundles by default, or as an opt-in for customers with HSM requirements?
